item.title: Hits close to home
item.content:encoded:
+1

As someone who actually played the kind of wargames this story is lampooning paying homage to, I loved this. If you ever played World At War or any of those pre-1980's Avalon Hill board wargames, then you've probably had plenty of conversations like this.

I mean the serious wargames. GTFO Axis and Allies. I am talking Seige of Jerusalem, Tactics, Third Reich, War and Peace. You've played the kind of game I'm talking about if you ever had:

  • cardboard chits for individual units
  • separate values for offense, defense, and movement
  • no less than a dozen charts for combat resolution
  • no less than ten pages of introductory historical essays to give you the "flavor of the time"
  • arguments about the armor penetration of anti-aircraft artillery
